title: Preparation of Testicular Cells for Immunofluorescence Analysis of Manchette in Elongating Spermatids
author: Changmin Niu

steps.title: Prepare all solutions
steps.instruction: Make fresh solutions as follows: Isolation buffer – add 5 µL DNase I (1 µg/mL final) and 2.5 mg Collagenase IV (0.5 mg/mL final) to 5 mL DMEM; 1× PBS – dilute 100 mL 10× PBS (10 % v/v) with 900 mL ddH₂O; Fixation solution – dissolve 4 g PFA in 50 mL 1× PBS, adjust pH to 7.7 with NaOH, then add 3.423 g sucrose (0.1 M) and bring to 100 mL with 1× PBS; Permeabilization solution – mix 10 µL Triton X‑100 (1 % final) with 990 µL ddH₂O; Blocking solution – combine 1 mL goat serum (10 % final) with 9 mL 1× PBS.

steps.title: Isolate mouse testes
steps.instruction: Set up a clean, well‑lit dissection area; anesthetize male C57BL/6 mice with CO₂ until unconscious (no movement when tapped); sacrifice by cervical dislocation; place mouse abdomen up, cut lower abdomen, remove testes and trim off fat and epididymis; wash testes in cold PBS, then transfer to fresh cold PBS to remove tunica albuginea; cut testes into tiny pieces and transfer into a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL isolation buffer.

steps.title: Digest tissue by shaking incubation
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a 32 °C water bath and shake gently at 50 rpm for 8 min, blowing tissues off the bottom with a transfer pipette every 3 min; repeat this shaking cycle three more times (total 4 × 8 min = 32 min) until tissues are fully dissociated.

steps.title: Centrifuge digested cells
steps.instruction: While waiting, cool the Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge to 4 °C; then spin the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash and re‑centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, add 5 mL 1× PBS and gently resuspend cells with a transfer pipette; centrifuge again at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL fixation solution, gently resuspend, and shake at room temperature on a platform shaker at 50 rpm for 15 min.

steps.title: Post‑fix washing and density check
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant and wash three times with 1× PBS; resuspend cells in PBS at 1 × 10⁵ cells/mL (range 1–2 × 10⁶ cells/mL for sperm); add 50 µL cell suspension to 500 µL fresh PBS; pipette ~10 µL of this mixture into a Petri dish and examine under a microscope to confirm appropriate dilution.

steps.title: Prepare slides with cell suspension
steps.instruction: If cell density is appropriate, draw a square on a positively charged slide with a PAP pen; plate 50 µL of the cell suspension onto each square and gently smear to fill the square, leaving the slide horizontal.

steps.title: Air‑dry slides
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the cell suspension on the slide for 45 min to 1 h; ensure the area is still slightly wet with no excess liquid, avoiding complete drying or excessive moisture.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells on slides
steps.instruction: Place slides in a humid (wet) box; add 50 µL Triton X‑100 (1 %) to each square and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Wash cells gently three times with 1× PBS; add 50 µL blocking solution to each square and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min in the wet box.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Remove blocking solution with a 100 µL pipette; add the indicated primary antibodies to each square and incubate overnight at 4 °C in the wet box.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation and final washes
steps.instruction: Wash cells three times with 1× PBS; incubate with the appropriate secondary antibodies at room temperature for 1 h in the wet box; wash three more times with 1× PBS for a total of 15 min; gently dry the slide surface with a Kimwipe.

steps.title: Mount slides with DAPI
steps.instruction: Add VECTASHIELD® Antifade Mounting Medium with DAPI onto each square, slowly place a coverslip, seal edges with nail polish, and keep the slides protected from light.

steps.title: Image slides
steps.instruction: Observe and capture fluorescence or confocal images of the stained cells using an appropriate microscope.
